# Login vectors

`login.json` contains invented email and phone accounts, a fixed timestamp, and
the expected form, encrypted body, verification headers, and login response.
There is no real account or vehicle data here.

The ciphertext and headers were generated by executing `encrypt_request` and
`encrypt_response` from the Python client's `net/crypto.py` at commit
`8ab0634b292e64f5198d979636e01616ea6af34f`, with that revision's `crypto_utils.py`
and `net/utils.py`. Python's `urllib.parse.urlencode` encoded the login forms;
`hashlib.sha1` hashed the synthetic passwords. PyCryptodome supplied the AES
implementation. No HTTP requests were made.

The timestamp is `1735689600123` milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The API root
is `https://example.invalid/api.app/v1/`, the request path is `/oauth/token`, and
the tenant and region are the MG Europe defaults. The prior token is empty.
All other inputs and outputs are recorded in the JSON.

Keep these expected outputs independent of the Rust implementation. Regenerate
them with the pinned Python source if the inputs change. See
[Third party notices](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for its license.

## Command vector

`command.json` contains only synthetic data. It was generated with Python
`hashlib`, `hmac` and `cryptography` AES-CBC/PKCS7, following `net/crypto.py` at
`5ffd4e2bbb501d1afbfb272d1f546c0dd2030d0e`. Its plaintext uses compact, sorted
JSON; the token is included in the key prefix and HMAC input. The VIN hash is
SHA-256 of `SYNTHETICVIN00001`. The generator is `generate_command.py` and does
not make network requests.

`read.json` is a synthetic empty-body GET signature vector, including the hashed
VIN query string. Regenerate with `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_read.py`
(standard library only). It follows `net/crypto.py` at revision
`5ffd4e2bbb501d1afbfb272d1f546c0dd2030d0e`. Read payload fixtures are inline
in the Rust specs and contain only synthetic data.

## Climate payloads

`climate.json` is generated offline by `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_climate.py`.
It ports the payload rules from Python client commit
`5ffd4e2bbb501d1afbfb272d1f546c0dd2030d0e`, `api/vehicle/climate/__init__.py`.
It covers all named climate modes, all three AC flag choices, fan-zero
normalization, and byte/profile boundaries. All inputs are synthetic.
Temperature profile ranges come from the gateway revision recorded in
[climate documentation](../../docs/climate.md). Invalid inputs are tested in
Rust and CLI specs; they never produce a request. Attribution is in
[third-party notices](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Independent heaters

Regenerate `heaters.json` with `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_heaters.py`
(standard library only, no network). It covers on/off payloads for rear-window
and steering-wheel heating, including marker presence and absence. Sources and
the intentional steering-wheel difference from the pinned client are recorded
in [climate documentation](../../docs/climate.md) and the generator. All inputs
are synthetic; expected payloads are independent of the Rust implementation.

## Locks and tailgate

Regenerate `locks.json` with `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_locks.py`
(standard library only, offline). The five synthetic payloads distinguish lock,
door unlock, latch release and powered open/close, including null parameters
and marker presence/absence. See [sources and semantics](../../docs/locks.md).

## Find-car

Regenerate `find_car.json` with `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_find_car.py`
(standard library only, offline). Four synthetic payloads cover lights only,
horn only, both and stop, including every flag and the protocol marker.
See [sources and settings](../../docs/find-car.md).

## Charging controls

`charging.json` is generated offline by `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_charging.py`.
The generator records the pinned Python and gateway revisions. It covers four
independent actions plus synthetic completed, rejected and pending responses.
No credentials, vehicle data or production captures are used.

## Charge target and current limit

Regenerate `charge_settings.json` with
`python3 tests/fixtures/generate_charge_settings.py` (standard library, offline).
The pinned current-client mappings cover all seven target percentages and four
current limits, including ignore codes that preserve companion settings and
invalid input examples. See [charging documentation](../../docs/charging.md).

## Charging schedules

`charge_schedule.json` is generated offline with
`python3 tests/fixtures/generate_charge_schedule.py`. It records synthetic
reservation payloads from client `5ffd4e2bbb501d1afbfb272d1f546c0dd2030d0e`
(`set_schedule_charging` and its schema), covering all modes, midnight,
overnight and equal bounds, and invalid times. Capability behavior follows
gateway `ec814eca135792d8202dfd29d6e443b53746d2a1`
`drivetrain_charging_schedule.py`. No production captures are used.

## Battery heating

Run `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_battery_heating.py` offline to regenerate
`battery_heating.json`. Python's standard-library datetime and zoneinfo reproduce
the pinned client's next-occurrence conversion with synthetic dates and zones.
Fixtures include on/off, disabled schedules, fixed offsets, rollover, DST gaps,
ambiguous hours and invalid inputs. No production data or credentials are used.

## Windows and sunroof

Regenerate `windows.json` with `python3 tests/fixtures/generate_windows.py`
(standard library only, offline). It covers every nonempty selector set for
open/close, all four helpers including all door actions, empty/duplicate
selections and invalid CLI combinations. The synthetic VIN hash verifies the
shared transport hashes once. Payload rules come from the pinned current
client; local validation choices are identified in the generator.
See [window sources and limitations](../../docs/windows.md).
